title: [Chapitre] III. Réseaux via découpages : notes manuscrites (08/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting, from the neighbouring pages: L is a set with a structure S_0 ⊂ P_2(L). In the totally ordered examples S_0 is the set of all 2-element subsets. There is a class Mod_f(L) of 'modular finite' subsets T. For each such T, the cofinite complement C(T) = L \ T is cut by an equivalence relation R_T into 'connected components' A. Each component A has a 'boundary' Ȧ ⊂ T, the points of T adjacent to A. The model case is on the next page: L is a dense line without endpoints, and T = {t1 < ... < tn}. Removing T leaves the open intervals ]-∞,t1[, ]t1,t2[, ..., ]tn,+∞[, with boundaries {t1}, {t1,t2}, ..., {tn}. The previous page treats the degenerate 'discrete' case, where R_T is discrete and every Ȧ is empty.

On this page Grothendieck sets out working axioms, possibly provisional, for this calculus of 'découpages' (cuttings):
(Dec1, finiteness) For every cofinite modular U = C(T), the set π0(U) of connected components is finite.
(Dec2, functoriality of components in the cut set) Let U = C(S) and V = C(T) be cofinite modular parts with U ⊂ V, i.e. T ⊂ S. Then every component A of U lies in a unique component B of V. Moreover the boundary is compatible: (Ȧ ∩ T) ⊂ Ḃ, where Ȧ ⊂ S and Ḃ ⊂ T.

In modern terms, Dec2 makes T ↦ π0(C(T)) a contravariant functor on the poset of finite modular sets, via the maps π0(C(S)) → π0(C(T)) for T ⊂ S. It also makes the boundary operator monotone under coarsening the cut. This is the combinatorial analogue of 'closure of A ⊂ closure of B'.

The purpose is an axiomatic, purely combinatorial theory of 'networks' (réseaux) obtained by cutting a space (line, graph, perhaps surface) along finite sets. It sits in the 1986 'réseaux / découpages' material, presumably connected to cutting surfaces along curves and to dessins/maps.
errors: No error. Dec2 is consistent with the line example: take S = {t0,t1,t2}, T = {t1}, A = ]t0,t1[. Then Ȧ ∩ T = {t1}, which lies in Ḃ = {t1} for B = ]-∞,t1[.
The containment part of Dec2 is automatic if connectedness is monotone, i.e. R_S is the restriction of R_T. It is stated as an axiom because R_T is abstract.
The definition 'Partie modulaire fermée' is crossed out and left undeveloped.

ideas.what: Finiteness axiom: the complement of any finite modular cut has finitely many connected components
ideas.modern_name: finiteness of π0 of complements; tame/o-minimal-style finiteness
ideas.usually_credited_to: standard in o-minimality (van den Dries et al.) and in tame topology generally
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses 'topologie modérée' only in general terms

ideas.what: Inclusion of components under refinement of the cut, with monotone boundaries (Ȧ ∩ T ⊂ Ḃ)
ideas.modern_name: functoriality of π0 of complements on the poset of finite cut sets; abstract cut systems / ends
ideas.usually_credited_to: standard; cf. Freudenthal ends, Stallings/Dunwoody cut theory

missed.claim: A provisional axiomatization of 'découpages' (cut systems with boundaries) for networks, with only the totally ordered line as worked example. It is not developed on this page.
missed.quote: On va faire des hypothèses ... peut-être provisoires
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is an abstract combinatorial framework for decompositions by finite cuts with a boundary calculus. It is reminiscent of later abstract cut-system and tree-decomposition theories, but this page contains only routine axioms.

deep.surprise_reason: Routine foundational axioms (finiteness of components, monotonicity of components and boundaries under refinement), stated provisionally. Nothing here would surprise a specialist.
transcription_corrections: 'partie modifiée' should read 'partie modulaire' (and the crossed-out heading is 'Partie modulaire fermée' rather than 'Partie modifiée fermée'), consistent with the previous page.
'Alors [?] composante connexe A' reads 'Alors toute composante connexe A'.
'Soient U' is written 'Soit(s) U', with the insertion '= C(S), V = C(T)' above.
Line 2 is uncertain; 'justifier dévissements' is doubtful, perhaps 'justes de dévissage(s)' or similar.
